review_type: Fresh-reader editorial simulation by the same assistant; not an independent blinded reviewer, a human grade or a new model evaluation.
overall_verdict: The section has a coherent research story and useful evidence. Its main editorial weaknesses are unclear experiment boundaries, duplicated explanations and dense tables. Several claims also need tighter separation between observed results and plausible explanations.
strengths: Clear progression from mT5 adaptation to meaning-preserving rewriting, larger teachers and compression.
Concrete datasets, settings, values and failure examples make the work substantive.
Appropriateness, local style and paired meaning are treated as separate objectives.
The latest distillation results use matched inputs and metrics and report uncertainty.
The account is candid about persistent errors and does not claim that every experiment succeeded.
reader_questions_to_resolve: Are the SEA-LION results in Sections 3.3 and 4 from the same checkpoint and the same conversations?
Did English-first rewriting alone cause the gain?
Did the dataset change, and are conversations being confused with reply targets?
What would count as a pass or a high score?
Why retain SEA-LION when Qwen also appears coherent and mT5 is smaller?
Has the dataset been shown to cause weak Singlish?
How many stages are there, and what does each one learn?
What extra learning does public adaptation provide before the small project set?

findings.issue: The report alternates between early mT5, later SEA-LION/Qwen teachers and the deployed V5 model without identifying them consistently.
findings.reader_question: Are the SEA-LION results in Sections 3.3 and 4 from the same checkpoint and the same conversations?
findings.recommended_change: Distinguish the historical V5 configuration (Section 3.5) from later 768-case teachers; distinguish 50-case development studies from the 60-case system evaluation.
findings.action_taken: Clarified in the larger-model and distillation sections; no peer results were edited.

findings.issue: The 20.3 to 46.0 meaning-preservation comparison changed both target alignment and generation order.
findings.reader_question: Did English-first rewriting alone cause the gain?
findings.recommended_change: Name both changes in the prose and table headers; do not present this as an isolated pipeline ablation.
findings.action_taken: Table 3.3b now identifies both conditions explicitly.

findings.issue: The sequence 190, 790, 768, 766 and 571 appears without a complete explanation of what was removed or counted.
findings.reader_question: Did the dataset change, and are conversations being confused with reply targets?
findings.recommended_change: Explain 190+600=790, 22 source exclusions, two extra rewrite exclusions and the common reviewed teacher subset of 571.
findings.action_taken: Added a compact provenance chain; checked against the frozen recipes.

findings.issue: Contextual appropriateness, adequacy, recognizable Singlish and willingness to send are used without short operational definitions.
findings.reader_question: What would count as a pass or a high score?
findings.recommended_change: Define relevance/constraints, paired meaning and local syntax; explain 1–5 judge scales and binary would-send ratings.
findings.action_taken: Definitions added; uncertainty is explicitly not a pass in the exploratory counts.

findings.issue: The conclusion gives an engineering preference but does not connect it clearly to the existing system evaluation.
findings.reader_question: Why retain SEA-LION when Qwen also appears coherent and mT5 is smaller?
findings.recommended_change: Connect the historical V5 choice to Section 4 while identifying later teacher/distillation work as follow-up research.
findings.action_taken: The revised ending retains SEA-LION and separates generator Qwen from the Qwen-based reranker.

findings.issue: “The issue was therefore uneven style supervision” sounds more causal than the descriptive audit supports.
findings.reader_question: Has the dataset been shown to cause weak Singlish?
findings.recommended_change: Use possible-contributor wording; distinguish target variety, inference copying and inherited teacher copies. Preserve the warning that particles and copy counts are not quality scores.
findings.action_taken: Causal wording softened and audit evidence retained with clear scope.

findings.recommended_change: Keep two conceptual stages with two public-data phases; remove internal numbering and briefly explain masked-span reconstruction.
findings.action_taken: Simplified stage explanation; corpus roles made explicit.

findings.issue: The rationale is useful but repeats the initial training description and ends with a lengthy defensive qualification.
findings.reader_question: What extra learning does public adaptation provide before the small project set?
findings.recommended_change: Condense into the progression multilingual pretraining → informal-language/reply adaptation → project-specific task; retain one sentence that necessity was not isolated experimentally.

findings.issue: Independent versus English-first generation is explained at the end of 3.3.1, again at the start of 3.3.2 and again around the figure.

findings.issue: Table 3.3d repeats the larger-model paragraphs without adding measured evidence or concrete outputs.

findings.issue: Six long design descriptions restate the expected purpose, followed by verbose descriptions of mixed outcomes.
findings.reader_question: Which change mattered, what happened, and why was it insufficient?
findings.recommended_change: Keep every reviewed experimental family, but compress each row to the intervention and its decision-relevant result.
findings.action_taken: All six families, representative numbers and failure examples retained in shorter rows.

findings.recommended_change: Keep four beams, repeated-three-gram blocking, token limits and the bounded qualitative reason for adoption.
findings.action_taken: Shortened while retaining the adopted decoding settings.

findings.issue: “Aligned soft distillation”, “different vocabularies”, “projection/alignment components” and “KL-only ablation” appear in quick succession.
findings.reader_question: How does the soft method differ from learning teacher-written replies?
findings.recommended_change: Explain text targets versus teacher probability information, why learned alignment is needed and that KD adds both an objective and alignment modules.
findings.action_taken: Simplified the explanation; preserved the confound.

findings.issue: The paragraph spends space on 3,390 requests, deduplication and successful execution before explaining the metrics.
findings.reader_question: Does the number of API calls establish stronger evidence?
findings.recommended_change: Keep matched inputs, blinded identities, persona correlation and averaging; leave operational request counts in the results artifacts.
findings.action_taken: Removed call-level bookkeeping from the school report; 5,000 rating cells and all scores remain.

findings.issue: “Not independent human ratings”, “reused development” and “not a conclusive replacement” recur throughout neighboring paragraphs.
findings.reader_question: Can the limitation be stated once without weakening the conclusion?
findings.recommended_change: Use one shared note for early exploratory counts and one distinct final paragraph for the automated study.
findings.action_taken: Consolidated qualifications while retaining their different meanings.

findings.issue: Near-5 naturalness scores and uniformly perfect English style scores can look like uniformly excellent replies.
findings.reader_question: How can a model score highly but still reverse roles?
findings.recommended_change: Explain that fluency is distinct from contextual correctness; a saturated style metric cannot distinguish systems.
findings.action_taken: Added this interpretation to the evaluation limits.

findings.recommended_change: Explicitly state they were not; retain the example as an illustration, not an aggregate ranking.
findings.action_taken: Clarified; a matched teacher evaluation remains a research requirement.

findings.issue: Two placeholders remain in an otherwise completed section.
findings.reader_question: Are these figures still missing?
findings.recommended_change: Supply the explanatory pipeline figure and use a concrete output table instead of the redundant second placeholder.
findings.action_taken: One embedded diagram and one real output table replace both placeholders.

findings.issue: CoSEM, DailyDialog, NUS SMS, LoRA and multiple model names arrive quickly; full hyperparameters compete with explanation.
findings.reader_question: Which details are needed to understand this section?
findings.recommended_change: Explain corpus/model roles briefly, retain the requested training table and distillation settings, and use Section 3.5 for the historical deployment configuration.
findings.action_taken: Scope clarified without changing peers’ methods or bibliography.

research_gaps_that_editing_cannot_resolv: No clean ablation removes only the original public-adaptation stage, so its necessity and isolated effect remain unmeasured.
The two teachers have not received the same matched judge scoring as the five students; a numerical teacher–student quality gap cannot be reported.
The dataset audit is descriptive; it does not establish the causal contribution of synthetic proportion, target style, decoding or regional pretraining.
The current judge schema does not measure English–Singlish consistency jointly, and no new blinded human local-style study has been run.
The repeated 50-conversation validation results do not establish untouched test performance or broad statistical reliability.
Varying teacher models and adding KD alignment components do not isolate regional pretraining or a single distillation loss term.
scope: Only section3.3 revised; other authors’ prose, reported metrics and references preserved.
